findings.description: `runGateChild` settles only on `'close'`, and Node emits that only after the process has exited *and* every stdio pipe has closed. On a timeout or an overflowing pipe, `stop()` only sends SIGTERM to the child's process group. On an interrupt, the kill timer only sends SIGKILL to that group. Neither closes pup's ends of the pipes. Suppose a process outside the group still holds the stdout/stderr pipe, for example a test that starts a server with `spawn(..., { detached: true, stdio: 'inherit' })` and never stops it (`detached` calls setsid). Then `'close'` never fires. The timeout fires once and nothing settles, so the gate hangs for good while holding the merge lock. Ctrl-C doesn't end it either: the forwarders and `withMergeLock`'s `stayAlive` keep pup alive, and the SIGKILL after the grace can't reach that process. The operator has to `kill -9` pup, which leaves `.git/pup-merge.lock` and the gate checkout behind. The old `execFileSync` (spawnSync) closed its pipe ends when it killed on timeout or overflow, precisely so that a grandchild holding a pipe could not hang it. So `GATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` always ended the stage as an ETIMEDOUT failure. This is a silent regression of the gate's only guarantee that it ends.
findings.body:
**A stage whose pipe outlives its process group now hangs the gate past its timeout, while it holds the merge lock**

`runGateChild` settles only on `'close'`, which Node emits after the process exits *and* all of its stdio pipes close. Nothing listens for `'exit'`. On a timeout or an overflowing pipe, `stop()` only signals the process group:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3bfbe9165faddb1ef3a09fe0cc5427a7507aaf3c/src/core/sandbox.utils.ts#L233-L243

The interrupt path's SIGKILL escalation (around L426) also only signals the group. A process that left the group (`setsid`, e.g. a test that leaks a helper spawned with `detached: true, stdio: 'inherit'`) but still holds stdout or stderr stops `'close'` from ever firing. The same happens when a same-group process traps SIGTERM, because timeout and overflow never escalate to SIGKILL. When that happens:

- The timeout fires once and changes nothing. The stage never settles, so the merge lock stays held indefinitely.
- Ctrl-C is forwarded and the 5 s SIGKILL reaches only the group. pup's own listeners keep it alive, so the operator has to `kill -9`, which leaves `.git/pup-merge.lock` and the gate checkout on disk.

`execFileSync` didn't have this problem. spawnSync's `Kill()` always calls `CloseStdioPipes()` on timeout and on maxBuffer overflow, so a timed-out stage always came back as an `ETIMEDOUT`/`ENOBUFS` failure. To restore that, close pup's ends of the pipes whenever it stops a child. Below is the `stop()` change. The `forwardInterrupt` kill timer needs the same two `destroy()` calls after its SIGKILL.

findings.description: `coveredTest` decides whether to fold by reading only `ctx.configPath`, which is the trusted main checkout. Before this PR, the gate's test stage was `{ command: pm, args: ['run', 'test'] }` run with `cwd` set to the gate checkout, so the package manager ran the session's own `scripts.test`, `pretest` and `posttest`. The folded run is `npx --no-install vitest run --coverage…`, which never reads the checkout's scripts. So if a session edits its own test script, the gate tests something other than what the script runs. That is exactly the case the code comment says folding must avoid.
findings.body:
**The folded run checks only the trusted scripts and config, but the old test stage ran the session's own script**

All three folding checks read `ctx.configPath`, the trusted main checkout:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3bfbe9165faddb1ef3a09fe0cc5427a7507aaf3c/src/adapters/typescript.adapter.ts#L400-L413

On main, the gate's test stage was `pm run test` with `cwd` set to the gate checkout (`commandStage('test', test, checkout)`). The package manager therefore ran the **session's** `scripts.test`/`pretest`/`posttest`, and the trusted manifest only decided whether the stage existed. Once `merge-gate.service.ts` replaces that with `{ ...test, ...covered }`, the session's script is never read. Decision 95 justifies folding with "Anything else would make the instrumented run a different run from the one the script makes". When a session edits its script, it gets exactly that different run:

- **False pass:** the session sets `"test": "vitest run && playwright test"`. The e2e step never runs in the gate, then becomes main's script on merge.
- **False fail:** the session adds a `pretest` codegen step, or `coverage.thresholds` to its own vitest config. The step is skipped, or a figure fails a suite whose tests all passed. Decision 94 then re-runs it and reports it as "failed twice — none named in its output".

Applying the same checks to `ctx.measurePath` as well can only *reduce* folding, and every decline falls back to the pre-PR two-run path, so a session gains nothing from it. Wrap the read in a `try`: the measured `package.json` is session-controlled, and `coveredTest` is called outside any `try` in `measureBranch`. In init, audit and land, `measurePath === configPath`, so nothing changes there.

findings.description: The change turns a private `interface MeasuredBaseline extends InitReport { gaps: DebtGap[] }` into an exported one so `src/core/audit.service.ts` can import it, which `docs/conventions/general.md` §Type separation forbids in a `*.service.ts` file.
findings.body:
**Exported interface added to a service file**

This PR changes `interface MeasuredBaseline extends InitReport { gaps: DebtGap[] }` to `export interface MeasuredBaseline …` so that `src/core/audit.service.ts` can import it:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3bfbe9165faddb1ef3a09fe0cc5427a7507aaf3c/src/core/init.service.ts#L169

`docs/conventions/general.md` §Type separation: "Exported types live in `*.types.ts` under the area's `types/` folder — `src/core/types/`, `src/adapters/types/`. **Never inline an exported `type`/`interface` in a `*.service.ts` or `*.routes.ts` file**."

`InitReport` already lives in `src/core/types/init.types.ts`. Move `MeasuredBaseline` there, next to it, and use `import type` in both `init.service.ts` and `audit.service.ts`.

findings.description: On main, any failure of the instrumented vitest run only degraded coverage to "not measured". With folding, two coverage-only failures now fail the test stage. First, coverage overhead can push a suite that passes plain past the shared 10-minute timeout. Second, forced instrumentation of every source file via `--coverage.include` can error on files the plain suite never loads. Decision 95 names only thresholds as a coverage-only cause.

`declaresCoverageThresholds` looks only for the literal `thresholds` key. Vitest before 1.0 declared thresholds as `coverage: { lines, functions, branches, statements }`, so a repo pinned to vitest 0.x would fold, and a figure would fail a suite whose tests all passed.

The `EXEC_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES` comment claims parity with execFileSync ("a child that floods a pipe fails where it did"). But execFileSync's `maxBuffer` limits stdout+stderr combined, while `collect()` limits each stream separately. A stage whose output totals 1–2 MiB used to fail with ENOBUFS and now passes. Either fix the comment or count both streams against one total.

`pup audit`/`pup land` now print `0.0s` for a skipped stage, because `measureStages` stores `durationMs: 0` for a stage with no command. Decision 95 says a stage that ran nothing has no time. Omit the time when `status === 'skipped'`, here and in `printInitReport`.

`writeProfile` uses its directory argument both as the profile's location and as its write-deny root. Each child's profile now denies only its own `policyDir/child-XXXX` instead of the whole policy directory, which weakens decision 36's "stays unwritable whatever a caller passes as writable" for sibling profiles. No current grant covers `policyDir`, so this is not reachable today.

The gate's "before" complexity child for a custom adapter runs with `cwd` set to the trusted checkout, which is granted writable, and it shares the toolchain cache and TMPDIR that session children can write. A poisoned cache could therefore run with write access to the trusted repo, against decision 36's "trusted checkout is not writable during a merge". This already existed; running stages concurrently only overlaps the two in time.

`initProject`, `measureBaseline` and `auditProject` return promises but are deliberately not `async`, and they gain the single-caller `measureStages`/`judgeAudit` splits. Both exist only so that the sync `runOrReportNoAdapter` guard still catches a thrown `NoAdapterError`. Making that guard `async` (`return await fn()`) would let these become plain async functions.

Nested-package results are split across `suiteResults` and `typechecks`, both keyed by a rebuilt `nestedStage(...)` string. They are read back with `as GateStageResult` casts that rely only on a comment's invariant. Keying by the `GateCommand` entry, or keeping one ordered list, would remove the casts. Line 1365 also still builds the label inline instead of using `nestedStage`.

`elapsedMs: Record<string, number>` repeats each judge's stage-name literal (`'dead-code'`, `'duplication'`, `'complexity'`, `'coverage'`) as untyped keys far from the judges, so a typo silently drops a timing. Type the key as a union of the stage names, or share the constants.

`formatDuration` is a report-display helper with no adapter caller (only core and cli use it). It belongs in `src/core/report-data.utils.ts` next to `displayStages`, not in the adapter-layer capability utils.

All three adapters' `coverage` catches now repeat the same tail: `if (error instanceof GateInterruptedError) throw error; return { unavailable: ... }`. The TS adapter also duplicates its message string from `instrumentedRun`. A shared `unavailableAfter(prefix, error)` helper next to `failureSummary` would make it impossible to forget the interrupt rethrow.

The new `GateInterruptedError` class lives in a `*.utils.ts` file ("pure functions only"). `general.md` places typed `Error` subclasses in a `*.errors.ts` file. `UndeclaredSandboxError` set the precedent, but the drift grows with each new class.
`printGateStage` takes the ad-hoc intersection `StoredGateStage & { durationMs?: number }`. Prefer the gate-stage type in `src/core/types/merge-gate.types.ts` that already carries `durationMs`.

The comment "`runMergeGate` is one synchronous pipeline that clones, installs, builds, tests and audits" is now stale: this PR made the gate async with concurrent stage children. Reword it to say the gate holds the CLI and prints nothing until it ends.
Decision 95 says "46 to 54% less than main's 585 s mean", but the branch's runs (275.4, 302.3, 313.7 s) against a 585 s mean give 46.4–52.9%. The top of the range is 53%, not 54%.

Two lines in decision 95 run far past the file's 100-column wrap, likely joined in a hand edit. The long "Tests:" paragraph is an inventory of test cases that will go stale and carries no decision rationale; consider trimming it.

The `commandError` comment says "the operator's instructions are in that message". That holds only for `UndeclaredSandboxError`: a `GateInterruptedError` message carries no instructions. Split the two cases in the comment.

The edited `commandStage` JSDoc ("Runs one hard stage to its result. A failed test\n stage runs once more…") is now awkwardly wrapped, and "to its result" adds nothing beyond the return type. Re-flow it or drop the clause.

A line in the `runGateChild` docblock is wrapped at about 120 columns ("...and throws without it. The invariant is about gate *children*, and"). This PR edits the same docblock, so re-wrapping it would be in scope.

process_issues.description: review-context was not spawned: the change touches no CI, HTTP, docker or settings surfaces (src/adapters, src/core, src/cli and docs/09-decisions.md only).
The reviewer reported that piped Bash commands were denied, and it did not audit the test files against docs/conventions/testing.md.
